transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've just been feeling tired all the time, and I don't seem to have any energy. It's been getting me down a bit, to be honest.
Can you tell me when you first noticed this tiredness, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
Oh, it came on gradually, a while back now. And yes — codeine makes me very sick, I can't take it.
How much does the tiredness get in the way of the things you normally do day to day?
It does get in the way quite a bit, really. I'm finding it hard to help my husband wash and dress in the mornings like I used to.
Could you tell me what medicines you’re taking at the moment?
I take a few tablets each day — something for my diabetes, one for my thyroid, and something for my indigestion that I've been on for years. And I buy some painkillers myself for my shoulder.
Would you say the tiredness is mild, medium, or severe, or you're not sure?
I'd say it's fairly bad — if I had to put a number on it, maybe a 3 out of 10 for energy.
Alongside the tiredness, have you noticed anything else different or new in how you feel?
I do get more out of breath than usual when I'm walking up hills, and a couple of friends have said I look a bit pale.
Where do you feel the tiredness most — is it all over your body, or more in one particular place?
It's not really in one place — it's just all over, a general lack of energy. It tends to be worse in the afternoons.
Is there anything that helps you feel less tired?
A bit of a rest helps for a short while, but it doesn't last. I've started needing a nap most days now, which I never used to.
Besides the diabetes, thyroid condition, and indigestion you mentioned, is there anything else from your past health that you think I should know about?
That's about it, really — just the diabetes and the thyroid, and the indigestion tablets. Nothing else I can think of.
What worries you most about this tiredness, and what are you hoping to get out of today’s visit?
I suppose what worries me most is whether I'll be able to keep looking after my husband. He's got Parkinson's and he relies on me, so I need to get my energy back.
Is there anything else you've noticed that you'd like to add?
Well, I've had to give up my swimming twice a week, which I miss. And I sleep about seven hours but still wake up not feeling refreshed.
When did you first notice the tiredness and low energy — did it come on suddenly, build up gradually, or are you not sure?
It built up gradually, over about two months I'd say. It wasn't sudden at all.
Have you started any new medicines or had any changes to the ones you take in the last couple of months, or are you not sure?
No, I don't think anything's changed there — I've been on the same tablets for a long while now.
Is there anything else about your medicines you'd like to add?
Oh, one thing — I do take those painkillers for my shoulder fairly often, most days really. It's been sore for ages.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
